# Codacabana: Tacto Negotiation Arena

An AI buyer that negotiates by e-mail with supplier bots and closes the deal with the lowest
total cost, or walks away.

Built by Team Codacabana at the European Hackathon League Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 October
2026, on the Tacto track. The buyer works for Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a fictional pump maker. Each
case is scored on how much of the possible saving it captures:
`(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`. Brief: [docs/challenge.md](docs/challenge.md).

![Pipeline monitor replaying a test run: prepare, negotiate, close and learn, with the live supplier thread beside it](docs/assets/pipeline-monitor.webp)

*The pipeline monitor in [`pitch/`](pitch/README.md) replaying a simulated case, with the live
supplier thread on the right.*

## How it works

**Code owns every binding number; the model owns words.** Prices, term sheets, accepts and
walk-aways are computed and checked with the arena's exact cost function (`total_cost`,
`must_haves_ok`). Models read, argue and write, but cannot change a figure.

| Stage | What happens | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Prepare** | Four specialist researchers (economics, persona, history, leverage) and a lead build one supplier brief. A supplier and a buyer subagent then rehearse the arguments into a playbook. | [`research.py`](buyer/research.py), [`rehearsal.py`](buyer/rehearsal.py) |
| **Negotiate** | For each supplier reply: the live analyst reads the mood and tactic, the decision engine sets price and terms, the writer turns them into an e-mail with claims cited by data ID. | [`analyst.py`](buyer/analyst.py), [`policy.py`](buyer/policy.py), [`economics.py`](buyer/economics.py), [`claims.py`](buyer/claims.py), [`writer.py`](buyer/writer.py) |
| **Close & learn** | The close gate accepts the cheapest valid standing sheet across suppliers, or walks. A debrief saves the outcome for the next similar case. | [`policy.py`](buyer/policy.py), [`memory.py`](buyer/memory.py) |

The [runner](buyer/runner.py) orchestrates each case: it answers the oldest reply first and
keeps every move inside the arena's 60 second clock, whatever fails. The agent branches on what
the data says about a supplier, never on a case or supplier ID.

Read more:

- [writeup/writeup.pdf](writeup/writeup.pdf): the two-page paper on the approach, with the system diagram
- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md): the module map of the running system
- [docs/design.md](docs/design.md): what the agent does and why
- [docs/learnings.md](docs/learnings.md): what practice showed, with evidence

## Quick start

Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```sh
git config core.hooksPath .githooks   # secret scan, no pushes to main, Entire hooks
uv sync                               # the agent, Tacto's arena kit, pytest, ruff
cp .env.example .env                  # fill in the keys below
uv run arena data                     # data package into data/package
uv run arena me                       # the key works: team and practice quota
```

| Variable | What |
|---|---|
| `ARENA_URL` | `https://arena.tacto.ai` |
| `ARENA_API_KEY` | the team key from https://arena.tacto.ai/apply |
| `ARENA_DATA` | `data/package` |
| `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_API_KEY` | the model, any OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint; optional `LLM_EFFORT` |

## Run

```sh
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                     # one sandbox case (free)
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10     # every hosted practice case (counts against the quota)
uv run buyer pull --set practice                  # finished sessions with trace -> logs/sessions/
uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v     # the Live Final: start before 12:00, leave it running
```

## Pipeline monitor

The screenshot above is a small web app that replays one recorded case step by step: which
component acted, what it decided, and the e-mails that went back and forth.

```sh
cd pitch && npm install && npm run dev
```

It plays a bundled trace from the local simulator, so it needs no API key. Details in
[pitch/README.md](pitch/README.md).

## Develop

Rules for people and coding agents: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

```sh
uv run pytest -q                 # our agent end to end against the local arena simulator
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .
```

## Repo map

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `buyer/` | the agent |
| `tests/` | end-to-end tests against `arena-sim` |
| `pitch/` | the pipeline monitor |
| `docs/` | brief, API, design, architecture, learnings, submission checklist |
| `writeup/` | the paper (`tectonic writeup/writeup.tex` builds it) |
| `analysis/`, `exports/`, `logs/` | exploration, Saturday's sessions as CSV, traces |

\begin{document}

\twocolumn[
\maketitle
\vspace{-2.2em}
\begin{center}
\begin{minipage}{0.88\textwidth}
\small
\textbf{Abstract.}
We describe ProcureCabana, an autonomous procurement agent that negotiates by e-mail with simulated suppliers
and concludes each case with either a single accepted term sheet or a withdrawal. Performance is
measured on total cost \C{} over the case horizon rather than on unit price; the agent therefore
optimises payment terms, delivery, contract duration, quality provisions and index clauses
jointly with price. The architecture separates two responsibilities. Deterministic code computes
every binding quantity and verifies it against the arena's cost function. A team of
language-model subagents analyses the supplier, rehearses the negotiation and composes the
correspondence, and its output is constrained by code before use. On the ten hosted practice
cases the agent concluded ten agreements with a mean score of 0.777.
\end{minipage}
\end{center}
\vspace{0.4em}
]

\begin{figure*}[b]
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.94, transform shape,
  font=\sffamily,
  box/.style={rounded corners=3pt, minimum width=3.4cm, minimum height=0.98cm, align=center,
              inner sep=3pt, line width=0.6pt},
  model/.style={box, fill=model, draw=modelline, text=white},
  code/.style={box, fill=code, draw=codeline, text=ink},
  arena/.style={box, fill=white, draw=ink, text=ink},
  wire/.style={draw=wire, line width=0.7pt, -{Stealth[length=5pt]}, rounded corners=2pt},
  bus/.style={draw=wire, line width=0.7pt},
]
  first round: one sandbox supplier countered at 51.30 without claims and at 50.00 with three.
  Claims a supplier judged irrelevant had no effect.
\item Final offers arrived at a cumulative gap of 36 to 42\,\% between our sheets and their
  counter-offers in four cases, and at 15 to 19\,\% for two less patient suppliers.
\item Bluffs and urgency left the price unchanged (three runs each), and all twelve suppliers
  asked declined to share a cost breakdown. The agent employs none of these.
\end{itemize}
After each practice case, code records the price trajectories and the score, and a debrief model
contributes one lesson, indexed by goal, case type, ownership type and observed traits. The lead
researcher is given the figures of the most similar earlier runs rather than the written lesson,
since a single run constitutes an observation and not a rule.

\section{Results and limitations}

One practice session per hosted case yielded ten agreements in ten cases and a mean score of
0.777. In that batch, 121 of 127 subagent invocations succeeded, and the six that timed out
reverted to the deterministic path. On the preceding evening the mean of our best scores per case was 0.776, third of 24 on the practice leaderboard.

Two limitations should be noted. First, a single batch does not constitute a paired comparison,
and we are unable to demonstrate that the subagent team outperforms the price engine alone.
Second, the full-cost estimate depends on a should-cost figure with a stated error of 5 to
15\,\%; the agent mitigates this by bounding the estimate with the supplier's own offers.

\end{document}

# Learnings

## Louis subagent-team practice batch (2026-10-11)

One hosted Practice session was run for each available case. All ten reached a deal; the mean
score was 0.7772. The dashboard reference at the time was 0.802, but this single batch is not a
paired comparison and does not establish a reliable gain or regression.

| Case | Score |
|---|---:|
| P01 | 0.9085 |
| P02 | 0.7347 |
| P03 | 0.9276 |
| P04 | 0.8604 |
| P05 | 0.8218 |
| P07 | 0.7313 |
| P08 | 0.7036 |
| P10 | 0.6785 |
| P11 | 0.7099 |
| P18 | 0.6957 |

The run recorded 127 subagent attempts, 121 successes and 6 timeouts; the writer had 37 attempts,
29 successes, 7 rejected paragraphs, 2 deadline skips and 1 timeout. Fallbacks kept sessions
running. These counts describe model reliability, not its effect on scores. The batch used the
`louis/subagent-team` base with the candidate safeguards; it is diagnostic evidence only.

Observations from the arena and the data package, with evidence. An entry says what happened and
how often, not what to do; what the agent does is in `design.md`. Most entries rest on one to
three sessions with one supplier. The sandbox bots are deterministic per sheet path; the practice
suppliers vary 1 to 2 % between runs with the same sheets. Sessions: `exports/` (schema in
`exports/README.md`), `logs/sessions/`, `logs/runs/`. Tags: `arena` seen in a session, `data` from
the package, `rules` from `docs/api.md` or the kit.

#!/bin/zsh
# Live Final launcher: at START (HHMM, default 1145) it freezes origin/main in its own worktree,
# runs the tests (falls back to the verified FALLBACK commit if they fail), records the hash and
# starts the final runner. DRY=1 stops the runner after 60 s (a rehearsal of the 403 wait).
REPO=/Users/stef/Projects/ehlcodacabana-final
RUN=/Users/stef/Projects/ehl-final-run
START=${START:-1145}
FALLBACK=d78759e
LOG=$REPO/logs/final-launch.status
say() { echo "$(date +%T) $*" >> $LOG; }

until [[ $(date +%H%M) -ge $START ]]; do sleep 10; done
say "launch (dry=${DRY:-0})"
cd $REPO
for i in 1 2 3; do git fetch -q origin && break; say "fetch failed ($i)"; sleep 5; done
git worktree remove --force $RUN 2>/dev/null
git worktree add -q --detach $RUN origin/main || { say "worktree on origin/main failed, using $FALLBACK"; git worktree add -q --detach $RUN $FALLBACK; }
cd $RUN
ln -sf $REPO/.env .env
ln -sfn $REPO/data data
rm -rf logs && ln -sfn $REPO/logs logs
uv sync -q >> $LOG 2>&1
if uv run pytest -q -x > $REPO/logs/final-pytest.log 2>&1; then
  say "tests pass on $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
else
  say "tests FAILED on $(git rev-parse --short HEAD), switching to $FALLBACK"
  git checkout -q --detach $FALLBACK && uv sync -q >> $LOG 2>&1
fi
git rev-parse HEAD > $REPO/logs/final.hash
say "runner start on $(git rev-parse --short HEAD) (hash in logs/final.hash)"
if [[ -n $DRY ]]; then
  uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v > $REPO/logs/final-dry.log 2>&1 &
  F=$!; sleep 60
  if kill -0 $F 2>/dev/null; then say "dry: runner alive after 60s, stopping"; kill -INT $F; sleep 3; kill $F 2>/dev/null
  else wait $F; say "dry: runner EXITED early: $?"; fi
else
  uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v > $REPO/logs/final.log 2>&1
  say "runner exited: $?"
fi
say "done"

"""Hero banner and numbers strip for the README, as self-contained SVG."""

import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

OUT = Path(sys.argv[1])
INK, INK2 = "#0F1724", "#1A2638"
ORANGE, SAND, MUTED, WHITE = "#F26B3A", "#F5D9B8", "#93A1B5", "#FFFFFF"
FONT = "Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif"


def waves(w, h, n=18, amp=26, period=220, phase_step=0.0, stroke=11):
    """Copacabana promenade: parallel sine bands."""
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        y0 = -40 + i * (h + 80) / n
        pts = []
        for x in range(-20, w + 21, 8):
            y = y0 + amp * math.sin(2 * math.pi * x / period + i * phase_step)
            pts.append(f"{x},{y:.1f}")
        out.append(f'<polyline points="{" ".join(pts)}" />')
    return (
        f'<g fill="none" stroke="{WHITE}" stroke-width="{stroke}" stroke-linecap="round">'
        + "".join(out)
        + "</g>"
    )


def banner():
    w, h = 1280, 420
    prices = [138.55, 134.10, 132.20, 131.10, 129.90, 129.70]
    # price ladder card
    cx, cy, cw, ch = 820, 78, 400, 264
    px0, px1 = cx + 40, cx + cw - 40
    py0, py1 = cy + 92, cy + ch - 58
    hi, lo = max(prices), min(prices)

    def pt(i, p):
        x = px0 + i * (px1 - px0) / (len(prices) - 1)
        y = py0 + (hi - p) / (hi - lo) * (py1 - py0)
        return x, y

    pts = [pt(i, p) for i, p in enumerate(prices)]
    line = " ".join(f"{x:.1f},{y:.1f}" for x, y in pts)
    area = f"{pts[0][0]:.1f},{py1 + 8} " + line + f" {pts[-1][0]:.1f},{py1 + 8}"
    dots = "".join(
        f'<circle cx="{x:.1f}" cy="{y:.1f}" r="4.5" fill="{INK}" stroke="{SAND}" stroke-width="2"/>'
        for x, y in pts[:-1]
    )
    ex, ey = pts[-1]
    sx, sy = pts[0]
    return f"""<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{w}" height="{h}" viewBox="0 0 {w} {h}" role="img" aria-label="ProcureCabana: the AI buyer that negotiates by e-mail and closes the cheapest deal on its own">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="bg" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="{INK}"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="{INK2}"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="fade" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
      <stop offset="0.25" stop-color="#fff" stop-opacity="0"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="#fff" stop-opacity="1"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <mask id="m"><rect width="{w}" height="{h}" fill="url(#fade)"/></mask>
    <linearGradient id="area" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="{ORANGE}" stop-opacity="0.35"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="{ORANGE}" stop-opacity="0"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <clipPath id="c"><rect width="{w}" height="{h}" rx="22"/></clipPath>
  </defs>
  <g clip-path="url(#c)">
    <rect width="{w}" height="{h}" fill="url(#bg)"/>
    <g mask="url(#m)" opacity="0.07">{waves(w, h)}</g>
    <rect x="0" y="{h - 6}" width="{w}" height="6" fill="{ORANGE}"/>
  </g>
  <g font-family="{FONT}">
    <text x="72" y="118" fill="{ORANGE}" font-size="17" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="3.2">EHL GRAND FINALE · MUNICH 2026 · TACTO TRACK</text>
    <text x="68" y="214" font-size="92" font-weight="800" letter-spacing="-3"><tspan fill="{WHITE}">Procure</tspan><tspan fill="{ORANGE}">Cabana</tspan></text>
    <text x="72" y="270" fill="{SAND}" font-size="27" font-weight="500">The AI buyer that negotiates by e-mail</text>
    <text x="72" y="306" fill="{SAND}" font-size="27" font-weight="500">and closes the cheapest deal. On its own.</text>
    <text x="72" y="356" fill="{MUTED}" font-size="17">No human in the loop. Every price checked by code. Every reply inside 60 seconds.</text>

    <rect x="{cx}" y="{cy}" width="{cw}" height="{ch}" rx="16" fill="{WHITE}" fill-opacity="0.04" stroke="{WHITE}" stroke-opacity="0.12"/>
    <text x="{cx + 28}" y="{cy + 38}" fill="{MUTED}" font-size="13" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="2">SUPPLIER'S PRICE, ROUND BY ROUND</text>
    <text x="{cx + 28}" y="{cy + 64}" fill="{WHITE}" font-size="17" font-weight="600">Volute casing · 8,150 units a year</text>
    <polygon points="{area}" fill="url(#area)"/>
    <polyline points="{line}" fill="none" stroke="{ORANGE}" stroke-width="3" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-linecap="round"/>
    {dots}
    <circle cx="{ex:.1f}" cy="{ey:.1f}" r="7" fill="{ORANGE}"/>
    <text x="{sx - 4:.1f}" y="{sy - 14:.1f}" fill="{SAND}" font-size="15" font-weight="600">€138.55</text>
    <text x="{ex + 4:.1f}" y="{ey - 16:.1f}" fill="{WHITE}" font-size="15" font-weight="700" text-anchor="end">€129.70 · deal</text>
    <text x="{cx + 28}" y="{cy + ch - 22}" fill="{MUTED}" font-size="14">5 rounds · <tspan fill="{WHITE}" font-weight="700">99.9 %</tspan> of the best possible saving</text>
  </g>
</svg>
"""


def strip():
    w, h = 1280, 190
    tiles = [
        ("10 / 10", "deals closed", "in the practice cases"),
        ("€1.19M", "saved", "against the opening quotes"),
        ("77.7 %", "of the best possible saving", "captured, on average"),
        ("10", "AI agents", "behind every negotiation"),
    ]
    tw = w / len(tiles)
    body = []
    for i, (big, label, sub) in enumerate(tiles):
        x = tw * i + 48
        if i:
            body.append(
                f'<line x1="{tw * i:.0f}" y1="40" x2="{tw * i:.0f}" y2="{h - 40}" stroke="{WHITE}" stroke-opacity="0.12"/>'
            )
        body.append(
            f'<text x="{x:.0f}" y="94" fill="{ORANGE if i == 1 else WHITE}" font-size="54" font-weight="800" letter-spacing="-1.5">{big}</text>'
            f'<text x="{x:.0f}" y="128" fill="{SAND}" font-size="18" font-weight="600">{label}</text>'
            f'<text x="{x:.0f}" y="152" fill="{MUTED}" font-size="15">{sub}</text>'
        )
    return f"""<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{w}" height="{h}" viewBox="0 0 {w} {h}" role="img" aria-label="10 of 10 deals closed; 1.19 million euros saved against the opening quotes; 77.7 percent of the best possible saving captured on average; 10 AI agents behind every negotiation">
  <defs><linearGradient id="bg" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="1"><stop offset="0" stop-color="{INK}"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="{INK2}"/></linearGradient></defs>
  <rect width="{w}" height="{h}" rx="22" fill="url(#bg)"/>
  <g font-family="{FONT}">{"".join(body)}</g>
</svg>
"""


OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
(OUT / "hero.svg").write_text(banner())
(OUT / "numbers.svg").write_text(strip())

![One negotiation replayed: the agents at work on the left, the e-mail thread with the supplier on the right](docs/assets/pipeline-monitor.webp)

One negotiation replayed: the agents at work on the left, the e-mail thread with the supplier on the right.

## How it works 1. **Prepare.** Before the first e-mail, a team of AI researchers studies the supplier's history, documents and costs, then rehearses the negotiation against a simulated supplier. 2. **Negotiate.** For every reply, an analyst reads the supplier's mood and tactic, code sets the price and terms, and a writer turns them into an e-mail that cites hard evidence. 3. **Close and learn.** Code accepts the cheapest valid offer across all suppliers, or walks away, and the outcome is remembered for the next similar case. ## Scorecard Share of the best possible saving each negotiation captured. 100 % is the cheapest deal the supplier would ever have agreed to. | Negotiation | ProcureCabana | Best of 24 teams | Tacto's own agent | |---|---:|---:|---:| | A foundry announces +9.5 % on pump casings | **99.9 %** | 99.5 % | 96.6 % | | A motor maker passes on rising copper prices | **73.5 %** | 84.7 % | 74.0 % | | Renewing the frame agreement for a frequency converter | **93.3 %** | 93.6 % | 92.5 % | | Renewing the ball bearing agreement | **86.0 %** | 87.4 % | 86.0 % | | Tender for the shaft of a new pump series | **82.8 %** | 82.4 % | 55.5 % | | Bundling the fastener kit with one distributor | **76.0 %** | 77.9 % | 78.2 % | | Alloy surcharge on stainless steel bar, distributor A | **74.8 %** | 91.6 % | 75.2 % | | Alloy surcharge on stainless steel bar, distributor B | **75.6 %** | 67.7 % | 38.6 % | | A seal supplier cuts our allocation | **71.0 %** | 70.2 % | 68.6 % | | Bearing brackets from a supplier with a red quality score | **79.4 %** | 80.7 % | 31.4 % | | **Average** | **81.2 %** | 83.6 % | 69.7 % | ProcureCabana: our best negotiation per case on the hosted practice set, as of Sunday 11 October. Best of 24 teams and Tacto's own agent: the practice board on Saturday night. The numbers above the screenshot come from a single run through all ten cases. ## Read more - [The paper](writeup/writeup.pdf): our approach in two pages - [The pitch deck](docs/slides/EHL_Codacabana_Slide_Deck.pdf) ## The challenge ProcureCabana was built at the European Hackathon League Grand Finale in Munich, 10 to 11 October 2026, for the challenge set by [Tacto](https://www.tacto.ai). Our agent buys for Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a fictional pump maker, and negotiates with Tacto's supplier bots. A deal is judged on its total cost over the contract, not on the unit price alone: payment terms, delivery, contract length, quality and index clauses all count. ## Team Codacabana - Steffen Grabert ([@stegra05](https://github.com/stegra05)) - Louis Heinrich ([@louis-heinrich](https://github.com/louis-heinrich)) - Julian Fritz ([@jfr77](https://github.com/jfr77)) - João Zuffo ([@Zuff2004](https://github.com/Zuff2004))
